questions.question: How do living things depend on sunlight, air, water and soil? Give one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Sunlight gives green plants energy to make food, and warms animals like frogs and lizards. Air gives oxygen for releasing energy and carbon dioxide for plants to make food. Water is needed by all living things: plants take it in through roots, animals drink it, and fish and tadpoles live in it. Soil holds plants up, gives them water and minerals, and is home to animals like earthworms.

questions.question: Give three ways that living things in an ecosystem depend on each other, and one way they change the non-living parts.
questions.expected_answer: They depend on each other for food, like herons eating frogs; for shelter, like weaver birds nesting in reeds; and for pollination and spreading seeds, like bees carrying pollen. They change the non-living parts, for example plants give off oxygen, roots hold the soil, earthworms let air and water into the soil, and dead plants and animals rot and add nutrients.

questions.question: Explain how a drought or pollution could affect the whole ecosystem at a farm dam.
questions.expected_answer: In a drought, the dam shrinks and the vlei dries out, so reeds die back, tadpoles cannot grow, there are fewer frogs, and herons have less food and leave. If fertiliser pollutes the dam, algae grow fast, and when they die and rot they use up the oxygen, so the fish suffocate. Because everything is linked, one change affects many living things.
